utterances.text: Most probably they saw us. How else would they have known?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I will take you back briefly to the time that Fatima Osmanovic was shot. Were there any other neighbours or other people, other women that you knew, present at the time that she was shot that you now remember?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: She was with me at the time. It was only Fatima Pedisa -- Hata Pedisa, and she was with me so we waited for Fatima to cross the street to go to the other side, but there was nobody else. During the war, people would not move too much because they were shooting. Only perhaps the people who were perhaps a bit more daring would go to fetch water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Hata Pedisa related to Ramiza Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: The mother of Ramiza Kundo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how old is Hata Pedisa?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to my evaluation, I think she would say she was born in 1933, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I ask the witness be shown, and indeed that we all see, Exhibit P3279X.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at your screen, Ms. Menzilovic, and in a moment you should see a photograph of a street. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that street?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I do recognise the street. This is our street, the street that we took to go to the city. So, yes, this is the upper part, the part that was over my house and I think this was the street that we were crossing, if I see it well. I think this is the road we had to cross to go to the well and come back from the well

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will move the photograph slowly to the right. Please continue to watch it. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to your answers in relation to one of the photographs you saw earlier, P1812, do you see in the photograph the house of Ramiza Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we can see two dwellings with roofs, one to the left of the pole and the other to the right of the pole. Which of the two is it or is it both?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: On the left side, just behind the tree, this is the house of Ramiza Kundo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will continue to move the photograph to the right. Please stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we now see, having regard to your earlier answers, the area where you and the other woman, the other women, rather, would take shelter alongside the garage which no longer exists?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to move the image to the right. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when that garage was there, did it -- did the front of the garage coincide with the front wall of the building that we now see with the glass or did it extent further out or was it further back?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: That garage was right next to this road. I can't tell you what length it was. The house was behind it, because the garage was right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look again to the photograph to your right, that is, the photograph on the machine to your right. Do you see that immediately in front of the silver car which is parked in front of the house, there is a black line drawn on the photograph. Do you see that? Very close to the shadow of the car.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: To the right? Do you mean to the right with respect to me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it is difficult to pick up on the photocopy. If we can show you the original. Immediately beneath the wheels of the car, do you see now the black thick pen mark, especially beneath the front wheel of the silver car?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about this? I do see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to it again?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the one? That line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Does that line have any significance in terms of the front of the garage?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I think so. The garage must have been somewhere here. I don't know. I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please look again at the screen and we will continue to move the photograph to the right. And perhaps that photograph can be returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps while that is being done, Mr. President and Your Honours, my learned colleagues and yourselves could look at the original photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not necessary, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was not only useful to see the front of the photograph, Mr. Ierace, but also useful to look at the back of the photograph which clearly indicates that it is not a stamp, but it is the ink of the marking on the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I showed it to my friend during the break and he now has no issue with that, as far as I understand

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will continue to move the photograph to the right. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on the photograph at the moment the area of Polje, having regard to your earlier answers?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, but it is at a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, there is what appears to be a power transmission pillar on the right and the house on the left. We will now continue to move the photograph to the right. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The pillar or tower is now to the left of the photograph and some vehicles appear in the photograph, blue and red. Mrs. Menzilovic, I would like you to tell us, when you cross the road, where you would then go in order to get to the well. Do you understand the question? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Once again, terribly sorry to interrupt but it is because of the interpretation that I am intervening. I think I heard in the French interpretation when the witness gave an answer with regards to Polje, I believe that I heard "field" or -- and I do not think that the witness said that in her own language. I do not see it in the English transcript either, so I just want to be sure that we are talking of the same place, and this is the reason why wanted to make sure that everything is clear with regards to the word "Polje."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think perhaps those of us who speak Bosnian our Serbian would have some understanding of this, given the witness's earlier answers. Perhaps I could clarify it, if is convenient to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That the witness testified that "polje" means "field."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but since we talked about a field, which is what I thought I understood in French, and while we were talking about the field, we were seeing a field that the backdrop on this 36-degree picture, that as a general term is -- there is an objection to it. A permanent objection stands. Yes, it is true that "polje" means "field," what I heard in French is the word "crete," which means something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I am certainly aware that proper attention will be given to the final production of the transcript in respect of this issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Menzilovic, we will continue to move the photograph slowly to the right. As we do that, as soon as you see the place where you would make your way to the well after crossing the road, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It is just behind this -- in fact, the area -- the thing that is between the blue and red cars, we would cross past through here and we would go down to the place where we got water. As to how far the well was from this location, I don't know exactly, but it wasn't very far.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will continue to move the photograph to the right in order to move us back to the starting position. Thank you. All right, you can stop there. No further questions at this stage, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, please proceed. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, you started answering questions by my colleague by telling us that at the location where you went to fetch water in 1993, Haska Dudevic was shot?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what month was it?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in July 1993. It was sunny. It was -- indeed, the sun was very hot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you were at the time when Haska Dudevic was shot?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I was at the well and Haska was heading towards well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I think it may have been around noon, maybe sometime past noon, but that would be it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the incident in which as you say Haska Dudevic was hurt, were there any other people there at that location where you were?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: There were two other women with me who had come down together with me and she was going down, too, and that was it. Nobody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you go to the well to fetch water?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It would depend on when my turn would come. Sometimes I would go there once every 24 hours; sometimes I would go twice in the 24 hours. It would all depend on how crowded it was. But in daytime, it was less crowded and I would use this opportunity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that people came to that well every day to get water and that it was crowded and people had to wait in lines?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That part of the city, the street and this whole area where you lived, can you please tell us what is it called?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It is called Brijesce. The name of my street when I arrived there was called Brijesce Cikma number 6, and now it is called Bulbulistan number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day when Haska Dudevic was shot, in that area where you lived, was there any shooting there, and how often would there be shooting?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It would depend. If they saw somebody, they would fire more frequently from sniper rifles. But there was quite a lot of shooting. That was the biggest problem we had in that part of the town, the snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period, so we are talking about 1992, 1993, 1994, did you see Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day when Haska Dudevic was hurt, did you notify the competent police authorities or anyone from the BH army that the injury took place?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Somebody went to the well from up there and we shouted at that person, "go back, go back, she has been hurt." And that person went back. I don't know who that was. I went to Haska to bathe her with water, to be with her, and then somebody reported to the Civil Defence in Brijesce. But it took a long time, maybe an hour or two, because there was a lot of shooting for somebody to get there. When the shooting stopped, they just took her down to the stream bed, down to the gardens, as we called them, and they had to run because they had to avoid being seen. There were some palm trees there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you tell us that on that day the shooting lasted for a long time in that area where you went to get water?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When Haska was wounded, there was a lot of shooting, probably to prevent people from approaching her. At any rate, there was a lot of fire from sniper rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine the area, the part of the city from which the shooting came from?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It could only have come from Polje and from no other part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear on that day the direction from which the shooting came?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the area that you called Polje from that area where you went to fetch water?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I already said that I am not quite sure. I never measured it, but it may be about 500 metres as the crow flies. Maybe it is even less but I really don't know. I am just giving you an approximation. This would be my assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the direction which you specify as Polje and the area that you say was controlled by the Republika Srpska army, can you tell us where were the positions of the BH army, if any? So in relation to that area that you had described for us.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where the BH army was. I never saw them because I didn't have the opportunity to go there. But I did hear that it was somewhere near the road, maybe below the road, the Brijesce road. But as I said, I didn't see it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we show you the photograph 1812, P1812. If I may ask the usher to show this photograph, the Prosecution Exhibit 1812 to the witness. So it is 1812PA. Witness, to your right, there is the photograph that you have already looked at.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us and show us on this photograph the area that you claim is called Donje Polje, lower Polje?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: You go down this road and all this, this entire area down towards Rajlovacic, was called Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to this line that you are indicating now on the photograph that claim is called Donje Polje , where is the Bozina Pumpa and the BH army positions that you claim were down from the road?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: The Bozina Pumpa is located there towards Rajlovac - I don't know what the distance is here - and then this road leads up to our place. I don't know the distance, how far the Serbian army and the BH army were from each other. I don't know because I never went there until -- during the war, until the area was liberated. I never went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you tell us that you have knowledge that the positions of the BH army were down from the road?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and they protected us, at least, the Serbian army should enter the area because our part of the town was a Muslim part and it was inhabited by civilians, by women and children, civilians. That is what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you confirm that the positions of the BH army were in the vicinity of the road facing the positions of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I heard. But I never saw it because I never went down there. But they were there to prevent them from getting in. That is what I heard, so I don't have direct knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your daughter worked for the army, for the military?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that she worked in the kitchen, in the canteen?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a canteen. If you call the kitchen the canteen, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the kitchen where the soldiers took their meals was?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Where they took their meals?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Where did your daughter work?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It was in a part of the town near Buljakovo, and the kitchen was there, but as to where exactly it was, I don't know because I wasn't there. But it was there in the vicinity of the Orahovacka Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did your daughter go to work?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sometimes she would go there once in 24 hours; sometimes once in two days. Whenever she was working there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your daughter ever tell you what military unit of the BH army took their meals in the kitchen where she worked?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that they did not actually take their meals there. The food was prepared there and it was taken elsewhere, so they did not -- the soldiers did not go there to actually eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say that they did not eat there and that the food was taken elsewhere, do you mean to say that the food was distributed to the positions where the troops were?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your daughter ever tell you to which positions the food was taken to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never asked that question because I didn't have time. And it simply -- I was simply not interested in that. The only thing I wanted to do, that I strove for, was to find water, to find wood for fuel and to feed my children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to go back to your answers to the questions posed by my learned colleague from the Prosecution regarding the incident when Haska Dudevic was hit. Can you tell us whether after this period, and up to the time when you gave a statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor, did anyone take any statements from you regarding the injury of Haska Dudevic?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, this is actually now the first time, because I will be testifying on her behalf because she wants to claim a pension so... But that hasn't taken place yet and I never testified on any other occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us that in the year 2001 you spoke to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001? Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the 5th of May, 2001 and on the 1st of November, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly, but if it says that these were the dates, then it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you gave statements to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor, did you give any statements to any official authorities, by that I mean the police or any official organ of the Court, regarding the incidents that you just told us about, the incidents that occurred in 1993? You spoke about the incidents in 1993, so did you give any statements regarding these incidents?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, not until the investigators came, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of Mrs. Kundo, of whom you spoke, and Mrs. Fatima, do you have any knowledge of them ever giving any statements?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I never discussed that with them, so I don't know whether they gave any statements or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how it happened that the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor came to you and spoke to you and interviewed you about it because they never -- you said that you never spoke to anyone?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. It is possible that they proposed me -- the two of them proposed me for -- as a witness. I wouldn't be surprised if that happened. But anyway I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 1st of November, 2001 when you spoke to the investigators of the OTP, you were shown a photograph, Prosecution Exhibit P1811. It is the house that you just spoke to us about. Do you have that photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Which house? I don't know the house that you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is photograph P1811. It is the house with the garage.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it, but not very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours, I have 1811 -- 1811 that was used when Ms. Ramiza Kundo was questioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that photograph here with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It is actually 1812.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1812 has been used today, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you see this photograph? It is now to your right.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, can you confirm the lines that are drawn on the photograph? You see the black lines?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do see them, but I don't know what you mean. That is probably where the garage was, but I don't know what the black lines are for. But I do see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you draw the black lines on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I may have, but I don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you drew those lines, if you marked the photograph in this way with the black line, what did you want to do?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I repeat, I don't know. I don't know who drew the lines but probably this means that the building did not look like that, that the garage was there closer to the road. But that is the only thing I can think of. This building was not there and that is probably why it was crossed out. I can't see any other reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you now confirm that you did not draw the lines on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I say again, I don't know. I don't remember. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us that you signed this photograph on that day?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did sign this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet you cannot confirm whether you drew the lines or not?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, that is the third time you asked it. The question has been consistently been answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. But the witness answered to a different effect. The witness answered in such a way that I felt that she would be able to provide me with a specific answer, but as she repeated for the third time that she cannot remember, that concludes my questioning regarding this photograph. I have no other questions regarding it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in the course of the examination-in-chief, you told us that it was mostly women and elderly men who went to the well to fetch water?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where were the young men and men who were able to work and who may have been younger people, let's say people aged between 20 and 40?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. That didn't interest me at all. My husband was not at home so I did not ask any questions about any other people, younger men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Fatima Osmanovic had a son and that he was a soldier in the BH army, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: If that is what you know. If you know that better than I do. I don't know. He was somewhere, I don't know where. He was young and I know that he was killed. As to where, on what line, I really don't know. As I said, it didn't interest me. I had my own duties. Sometimes I didn't know where I was at all. I had a death in the family. My husband was in captivity for four years in Visegrad. So the only thing that interested me were my children. Nobody in the neighbourhood interested me at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that when your husband came from Visegrad where you say he was in captivity, that he joined the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I do know that when he recuperated, when he got treatment for this wounds, he went to the -- he joined the army. But when Sarajevo was liberated -- well, I'm a bit confused, I can't really say that. I know that when Sarajevo was liberated, he came home. I know that he was alive and well, and that is the only thing that matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he joined the BH army, can you tell us what military formation he joined and where the positions were where he went?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you that because I don't know that. Because when he came home, I never asked him where he had been. I was only happy to see him alive and well. As to where he was, where he went, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your husband joined the BH army. Can you tell us how often he went to the position?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, I don't know. He was out there. Sometimes I would hear from him only once in a year, in every year, through ham radio operators. You ask me for too much. It seems that you want me to know something that you cannot know at the time when you are surrounded, you are besieged, you can't find information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a statement, Mrs. Menzilovic, to the investigators of the OTP on the 5th of May 2001, and on page 2 of your statement, in B/C/S, pages 03031342, you stated, and I will quote from line 3 of your statement: "Witness please go ahead. He had gone to see his father during in Visegrad in 1992 and was taken prisoner. He wasn't a soldier at the time, but he did join the army after he escaped.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but as to where he went and what he did I don't know that. Because he was in Vogosca, I don't know where he went. I would hear from him once every year through ham radio operators and he had to join somewhere to survive. He couldn't just wander around. I think, but I don't know, but I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise, but didn't hear the term that the witness used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the last part of the answer was not audible. Could you please invite the witness to perhaps repeat when she said "I would hear from him once every year through the radio operators and he had to join somewhere to survive. He couldn't just wander around," I think and what comes is not being translated. You might have heard me as well. The last part of what you said could not be heard by the interpreters. So would you please repeat it, on from where you said "He couldn't just wander around, I think but" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he just had to join but I think he was also in the kitchen. I don't know for sure, but that is what I think. He was in Gorazde. That is all I know. Any more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you tell us that your husband was a member of the BH army and that he worked in the kitchen as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when your husband returned to Sarajevo and came home, can you tell us when it was, what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in 1990 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For ten minutes we heard questions about such as where was your husband positioned, how often did he go to that position. Now the witness is asked questions as to what happened on his return not only after the incidents but after the war. I object to the question and the questioning on the basis of relevance, given the response my learned friend on such occasions in the pest that goes to testing the credibility of the witness. I anticipate that in my respectful submission, this questioning can have no relevance to the credibility of the witness. And in any event the issue of credibility only arises if something is in dispute. While the accused was not present while these people were shot, we don't say that. In my respectful submission, it is not at all clear from this line of questioning or such questioning in the past about similar witnesses what is in issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you explain the relevance?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the relevance is the following: The reason for these questions are to verify the credibility of the witness. When I stated to the witness a portion of her statement that she gave to the OTP when he was captured he was in the war but he joined the army after he ran away. The witness never told us that her husband was captured, was and in prison, but that he went to the army in Gorazde so my last question was the following: When is it that her husband arrived in Sarajevo. Because during the examination-in-chief she told us she was alone with her children. From her statement given to the OTP members, we can see that he joined the army after he escaped. I only wanted to ask the witness if her husband came to Sarajevo when he joined the army, BH.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: My husband had been captured before but when he escaped, he was in the army as I did say that. But then he came back home in 1996, in the month of May. So after four years later --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. Ms. Pilipovic, if you would have asked this question to start with you continued questioning about the military duties of the husband of the witness for quite some time. I was a bit surprised and I didn't want to interrupt you, but already at the beginning, she clearly indicated that her husband was not in Sarajevo. So I was wondering what the relevance is of the knowledge of the witness of what her husband does at quite a distance where she indicated again and again that she only knew she would be in contact with him only once a year approximately, what the relevance of this question was. Of course, I didn't know whether there were any, so I think it could have been done more efficiently but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I must say that the witness spoke all the time of a husband who worked in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No I said right away that my husband had not been there for four years. When you ask me now if he joined the army it is obvious that I said yes, but before, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you could have asked a kitchen in Sarajevo or a kitchen elsewhere. The witness testified she was alone with her children. So the first question that would have been appropriate is to ask about the whereabouts of her husband and if she then would have given the answer that she gave later on, it would have been clear from the beginning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you, but my question put to the witness were to examine the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we can say that the witness was not honest during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything I went through I lived personally, I felt it personally. I only know when I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, this is comment on the answers of the witness and I allowed you to proceed to cross-examine the witness. Would you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness you told us earlier that an incident occurred during which Ramiza Kundo was wounded?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when did this happen on what day and what was the date of the incident?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know the date. I know that it was the beginning of the month of November, but I couldn't really tell you the exact date because I didn't take note of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you go to fetch water with Ramiza Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I said that sometimes we wept once every 24 hours; sometimes twice. Other times once, but I couldn't really tell you how often, exactly. I know that I went to fetch water not only with Ramiza but as soon as somebody was going to fetch water, I would go with that person so that I don't go alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on that day when Mrs. Ramiza Kundo was injured, did you go to fetch water or were you coming back?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: We were coming back from the well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could we please show the witness the piture 1812A. Witness, you see a photograph on the ELMO. You already had seen this picture. Can you confirm to us if on this picture you see two containers?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us concerning these two containers, where were the two of you when Mrs. Ramiza Kundo was injured, how close to these containers were you?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: We were almost crossing already. We were to cross and this is approximately where we were when we hid. And we were just about to cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, was Mrs. Kundo to your right or to your left?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't really tell you. I don't remember because we were running and I don't remember any more. I do repeat that if I knew that I was going to testify here, that I was going to survive, I would have taken everything down in writing and you unnerved me so much because you told me I didn't tell the truth. Everything was the truth. I do not invent anything. I do not lie. These are the events I went through. I lived them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. With regards to these two containers, we can see a settlement just behind the containers. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if this part of the settlement also belonged to Brijesce Brdo?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but the streets are different. But I cannot tell you. Some people call it Brezanska. But yes, it does belong to that settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To Brijesce Brdo?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes. I don't know, but mainly yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the backdrop of this picture, in the area where we see a line between the blue sky and the settlement, do you see a mosque?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Where do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the lower picture just above the containers.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, if you know if during the year of 1993 in this part of the settlement, was there a tank?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never heard of that, and I don't really know. I have never seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if in or around this settlement during the conflict that lasted during the year of 1993 and 1994, if they were -- if there were any positions of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We talked about a settlement, an area that we can see on the lower picture right behind the containers. Could you confirm to us whether if in 1992, 1993, and 1994, positions of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were there?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: If you are talking about this picture in which we can see the containers, I can say no, the positions were not there. It was a settlement inhabited by civilians. There were no positions there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know, with respect to this part of the settlement that we see here, where were the positions of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know where they were. This is a civilian settlement under the road, and I can't see it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, you are telling us once again that you do allow the possibility that the position of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina could have been under this road?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is something that I had heard only, but I had never seen them. I had never gone there during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we talk about 1992 and 1993, as well as 1994, while you were going to fetch water and while you were waiting in line to get water during the day and during the night, would you sometimes see soldiers belonging to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the settlement where you lived?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see them there personally; and where I lived, I didn't see any. Maybe they were somewhere else, but not where I lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever during that period of time at any time see any soldiers? And could you also tell us how were they dressed, any soldiers of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really tell you. I know they were wearing camouflage uniforms but only when I would go to visit my sister in Pofalici. She was sick, and I would go and see her to help her. This is the only time when I would see them, when I would see them on the road to Pofalici because I would go on foot. But in my settlement where I lived, no, I have not seen them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Menzilovic, did you ever go to Mrs. Ramiza's house? Aside from going to fetch water with her, do you know who were the members of her family?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: With regards to Mrs. Ramiza Kundo, I have to tell you that I was her best friend. She had two daughters. One of her daughters was retarded; the other one is normal. And she also had a husband. And that is all. That was her family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, the husband of Ramiza Kundo in 1992, 1993, and 1994, do you know if he was a member of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that, and I also do know that he was also working in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the year of 1992, 1993, and 1994, had you ever seen the husband of Mrs. Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have, but not when he was wearing a uniform, and I don't know where he was going. My house was very exposed, and he was going somewhere behind. My house was the first one, as I said, the first one from Polje. You could see my house. My house was the first one to be seen. So nobody was able to come and go freely from my house and to my house, and this is why I can't really tell you. But I don't really know where he was going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Menzilovic, on that day, you say that it was the month of November when yourself and Mrs. Ramiza were coming back from the well. Can you tell us if the husband of Mrs. Ramiza was at home that day?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Hilmo Kundo was in the hospital because he suffered from kidneys, and the children were left alone. So when she went to the hospital, her mother stayed with the retarded kid because the retarded kid doesn't speak and she was crying a lot. That is why the third day, she had to come back from the hospital, because of her retarded kid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if when Mrs. Ramiza Kundo was wounded that day in November, that the police from the CSB of your locality, did they come to take any statements?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see them. Only when she was wounded, I called the Civil Defence. I don't even know how they were called actually any more. But no, the police wasn't coming there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Menzilovic, you see a picture on the ELMO. On the upper picture, you have indicated a house with a circle. Is this the case?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did indicate a house. This is Polje. This is where the shots were coming from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today during the examination-in-chief, in answer to a question by my learned friend, you said that you were taking care of the fields and you would hide when you would hear the shots?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Right under my house, Malbasic Savo, Janko, had a field, and it was a large field. And we would sow and dig, and we would work in the field but only during the night, never during the day. Sometimes also when it was foggy, I would go to look, and then I would hide back into the cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Menzilovic, on this picture, can we see this field that you were working on?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, we cannot see it. There is a photograph as showing a house; it is a newly-constructed house. It is the first house that we see right off the road, but we cannot see it on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you worked on the fields belonging to Malbasic Savo and Janko?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they also have that house or a house?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the son of Savo went to school with my eldest daughter for eight years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict, were you friends with them, with the neighbours, and were you working on the field together?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you worked on their fields. Did you work with them?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were not there during the war. They left right away, so they were no longer there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they own a house there?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did somebody live in that house, or was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody lived there. But yes, it is true that from their shells, maybe they thought it was our houses, the army of ABiH. But the house of Sava was incredibly exposed, and this is why nobody lived in that house. And now he sold that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if during 1992 and 1993, as well as 1994, on the positions of the army of BH, which under -- which according to your knowledge was under that road, do you know that they had weapons and did they shoot?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know this. As I said, I was not particularly preoccupied by this. I would like to say it one more time. I was not involved in military matters. I am a woman. I was taking care of my children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you were present when the incident involving the wounding of Fatima Osmanovic occurred?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you told us that she succumbed later?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when did she die?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I think she died 18 months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- the way in which that question was translated was by use of the word "succumbed". I would not like the Defence to think that it is the Prosecution's case that Mrs. Osmanovic died directly as a result of physical injuries suffered during this incident. I want to make that clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic. It might be the translation which suggested she finally died as a result of, I would say that could be the intrinsic meaning of the word used in the translation. But since whatever misunderstanding has been clarified, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which line, Mr. Ierace, are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about page 72, line 5, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. But since your colleague is cross-examining, if there is any specific question, I would rather avoid that it's two counsel at the same time. But that is the line where at least the translation of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. question is. I don't know what it was in the original language, but since everything has been cleared up, if there would have been a misunderstanding. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us on that day when Mrs. Fatima Osmanovic was wounded, were there any other people present at the well?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was waiting to cross the street with Hata, and then Fatima showed up. We didn't see anybody else. We waited for her to cross the road, and I saw her all of a sudden all covered with blood. I didn't see anybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if from the place where you were standing together with Mrs. Hata, at that moment when you saw Mrs. Fatima, can you see the source or the well from which the water comes from that spot?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, because it is under the hill. It is under the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us on that day when Fatima Osmanovic was wounded, was she transferred to a hospital, and which hospital was that, if so?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was transferred to a hospital and I believe it was the, Kosevo Hospital. I am not quite certain, though, that that was the case, that it was that hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the picture placed on the ELMO, and I am talking of the lower picture, are you telling us that the well was under the road?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It is across the street from the road, on the other side of the road, not completely under the road. But as we cross the road, we have to go down, and maybe 20 metres further down was that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, you had to go down 20 metres downhill to that well?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I never measured it. I am just giving you a general figure. Maybe it a 15 metres. I don't know. But I am just giving you a sort of rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the source was under, situated under the road?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: All right. If you wish to call it "under." I call it across the road. You call it under. Maybe we have a different way of saying things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you tell us and if we agreed on the fact that the well was under the road, and you told us that the positions of the ABiH army were under the road, would you be able to tell us at what distance were the positions from the ABiH army from the well?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you. I really don't know. It is in the direction of Polje towards the Serb side, but how far is it, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I tell you that when we talk about the well where you went to fetch water and if we talk about Polje, the area of the settlement for which you say that was occupied by the Serb army, so that if you look from the well, you would first see the positions of the ABiH army and then afterwards, towards Polje, you would see the position of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if in that area that we have identified the positions occupied by the ABiH army and the VRS, would you be able to confirm to us that there were battles fought between those two armies?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I never heard about this. I never heard them fight so I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us today during the examination-in-chief that shots were fired from the direction of the depot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at photo number 1 and photo number 2, would you be able to indicate to us where is this depot?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, because we cannot see it on this -- on these two pictures. It was not -- it is not present there. It is towards the gas station near Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic. Look at the clock. If you could find suitable moment to interrupt cross-examination. How much time would you still need, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 15 to 20 minutes at the most. This might perhaps be the right moment for a break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will have a break --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a headache and I would like to ask you for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will have a break for 20 minutes, and I hope that you feel better upon returning. If not, please tell us. Since I stole a few minutes from all of you during the first break, also from the interpreters, we will have a break until five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before you adjourn, feedback from Mr. Mundis, the proposal is acceptable to the person involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Facial distortion?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Menzilovic, I hope that during the break you had a moment to recover and that you feel a bit better now. Whenever there is any problem, please tell me, yes? Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to say that we are proceeding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first deal with the examination of the witness. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would now like the witness to be shown the circular photograph the Defence would like to ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we please have the assistance of the case manager of the Prosecution. I usually receive it on the computer evidence channel, which now shows an empty courtroom to me. So we will wait for a second. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is there any reason why -- I asked the technicians to teach you how to fix it again. Yes. I do understand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just so that as soon as you close your computer that the problem arises. So perhaps if you leave it open. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had some problems before. The computer was open when I addressed you, but I did not have time. But this is a habit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll ask one of the technicians to assist Mr. Piletta-Zanin now. Was that what you wanted to bring to my attention, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to turn your attention to two things: First of all, something happened during the break and my laptop no longer works, and secondly I wanted to say, but that is not important at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the laptop issue would have merited my attention. If then perhaps you start your first line my laptop is down again, then I know immediately that it is something serious which needs my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we usually rise and ask to be given the floor for some important matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would now like the photograph to be moved left in the direction left-wards. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Menzilovic, in the left-hand corner of this photograph we see a house which has an upper storey. Can you please tell us whether this house was there in the course of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: This one next to the one there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the first house that we see in the left-hand corner facing the pole.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, it wasn't there. There was a fence there where the meadow begin, that belonged to Janko.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think that description, for the benefit of the transcript, is ambiguous. Perhaps my friend could clarify which of the two houses which appear on the screen at the moment. Perhaps it might help that one of them is described as having a silver car in front of it, whereas the other car does not have any vehicles in front of it

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the first house as it was translated could be from this side or the other side. So...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, but I said quite clearly that it is the house facing the hole which is quite visible here in the middle of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any house there at all?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. The meadow began there. It was a large meadow and it belonged to Savo and Janko Malbasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you tell us there was a meadow down there where you tilled the land, where you farmed the land?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It belonged to the Malbasic family?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if this in photograph, in the bottom of the photograph, the little elevation, the hill that is seen here, can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Across the house, near the pole?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, near the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise but we didn't hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know what that hill is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think interpreters couldn't hear the answer but since the witness repeated it, I take it there is no unclarity any more. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you told us that the hill in the bottom of the photograph, which hill is it?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say anything. I don't know which hill you mean. What I see in front of the house towards the pole -- I can just see the flower beds belonging to the person that owns the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the bottom of the photograph behind the pole, do you see an inhabited area, a built-up area?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, further down deeper into the photograph. But I don't see a house or anything or a hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is this area that you can see in the depth of the photograph behind the pole? What is it called?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I see Polje. The whole area that I can see is Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Polje," does that mean the settlement of Polje?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it used to be a Serbian settlement before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the war?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war it was a Serbian area, and Serbs were there during the course of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that in the course of the conflict in Sarajevo that the area in the depth of this photograph was inhabited by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Serbs lived there. It was theirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in the bottom -- on the bottom of the photograph, this part that you referred to as a built-up area, the elevation that can be seen, can you tell us if this is a hill or a mountain, do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the big mountain in the back?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is Igman. It is the Igman mountain, if that is what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether in the course of the conflict in 1992, 1993, and 1994, whether there were any troops on the Igman mountain?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that and it didn't interest me. I said that right at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like the photograph to be turned right. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us as you look in the direction of this transformer behind this elevation where the road is, can you tell us in the bottom of this photograph, what part of the settlement is there? We cannot see it on the photograph, but can you tell us what is behind all this? What is in the bottom?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: When I look in this direction, and if we could see behind the blue van or whatever that is, you could still see the Polje settlement. But that is in the direction of Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us about the depot. Is the depot also located in this direction?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is in this general direction, but I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- you told us in the course of the examination-in-chief you mentioned Bacici, that this was also the direction from which the fire came from?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I never knew that this area, that this settlement was called Bacici. I knew it as "Polje". I had a little radio that I listened to from time to time. And I heard them shout they would open fire from Bacici. When I asked what Bacici was, I was told that it was, in fact, Polje, and that is where the fire came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that you listened to the radio, can you tell us, did you hear anything about the Bacici settlement and the settlement that you refer to as "depot," that there was any fighting going on there?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never heard it. I don't know whether there was any fighting going on. From what I heard on the radio, I only wanted to hear -- I wanted to hear news about anyone trying to liberate us, the foreigners coming in to protect us. Things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that -- if we look at this photograph, that in the bottom, that we cannot see that Polje is located there, is the Bozina Pumpa also located there?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps a little further down towards Rajlovac, but that would in general be it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm, then, that in the bottom -- at the bottom of this hill, behind this hill towards Bozina Pumpa, that the BH army positions were located there at the time?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm it. As I have already said, I didn't go there, and I wasn't preoccupied with the military things. The only thing that interested me was how to feed my children and my children in general. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please confirm that in relation to the place where you went to fetch water at the well, can you please confirm whether there were any trenches near that well?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, there were not any trenches there. I didn't see any trenches, and I am absolutely sure that there were no trenches in the vicinity of that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you say that you are sure that they were not in the vicinity, can you then tell us whether they were further away from the well? There were any trenches there, and how far were they?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were any, how far or what. I really don't know. I can't tell you things I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to have the photograph moved further to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you look in the direction of this car on this photograph at the top of the hill, do you see a mosque or a church?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I really can't see. I don't have my glasses on, and I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are two cars on the screen. Perhaps my friend might indicate whether she means the red car or the grey car.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. I meant the grey car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't really see because I didn't take my glasses so I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge whether if you look at the direction of the grey car, looking at the part of the settlement where in 1993 we have -- do you have any information that a BH army tank was there?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I never went there, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that witness Ramiza, Kundo who testified on the 22nd of March, on page 5966, when asked by the Defence about this part of the photograph, said that there was a BH army tank stationed there, would you agree with me that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't agree. First of all, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. The question has no probative value and the witness has already said she doesn't know. The fact that someone else has said there was can be of no assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you told us that in the part of the settlement where you yourself lived, you told us that Muslims lived there?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that there were no other members of other ethnic groups there in that part in the course of the conflict? I mean Croats and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: There were some Croats, but there weren't too many of them even before the war. They lived closer to their own church. But -- and perhaps 100 and 150 metres away from where I live, there was a Serb. He still lives there, in fact. But these were all the local inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When my learned colleague asked you this question, you explained to him that they would shout things at you - you said these were probably Serbian soldiers - as you repaired the roof to your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the photograph to be moved to the right, as far to the right as possible. To the right, to the right, not to the left. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the house of Ramiza Kundo which you identified for us, where and in what direction in relation to this house would your house be, and how far away from Ramiza Kundo's house it was?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: My house was straight down 20 metres. If you climb up the stairs and then look down 20 metres or so. I never measured it, but that would be it. It was the first house next to the meadow owned by Malbasic family, so the first house you can see here, and then there is another house and then my house. There was no house on the meadow. My house was the first house next to the meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to your house, can you tell us how far away from it were the positions of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, as I have already said, I never measured it, but as the crow flies, perhaps 500 metres. As I said, I never measured it. I never checked it but I have said this for quite a few times. I cannot tell you this with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you tell us that the positions of the Republika Srpska army were about 500 metres away from your house as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, approximately a bit more, perhaps a bit less, but that would more or less be it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that from that direction, from 500 metres away as the crow flies, that Serb soldiers shouted at you whether you needed any -- do you need any nails?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. They first destroyed the roof and then they asked us if we needed any nails.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the location of your house, were you able to see the positions and the location where the Republika Srpska army soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see the positions, I don't know where the positions were, but you could clearly see the area inhabited by Serbs from the terrace, Polje, the houses, I didn't see the soldiers, however, because during the day, I didn't even dare to look. But I know what the view is of Polje from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you can see the Serb houses from your house, can you tell us, the Serb houses, how far away from your house were they?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I already told you. Because these houses were in Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence doesn't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. President. First of all, the picture on the screen shows the light pole slightly to the left of centre and the passageway between the light pole and the house to the right. Mr. President, I was going to ask that a particular photograph be shown to the witness, but I notice it is already to her right on the ELMO. Re-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Menzilovic, would you look at the photograph on the bottom of the page just to your right. You were asked to indicate where you and Ms. Kundo was at the time that she was shot. Would you please take a blue pen and with a cross on that photograph, mark, where to the best of your recollection, Ms. Kundo was at the precise moment that she was shot? Just before that happens, Mr. President, on the video evidence button, I am not getting the ELMO. I don't know whether anyone else is. Before it is marked, perhaps we should clarify that, rectify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we please have under the video evidence button the ELMO because at this moment I see Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark that position with a cross.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Here on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Right here on this photograph, I can tell you only the place on the other side of the pole. So I can only indicate to you that place. So on the other side of the pole a little further down or up, if you wish, I cannot give you this indication from this picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see on the photograph where Mrs. Osmanovic was at the time that she was shot?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do see the spot. Right next to this tree, and Ramiza was a little further up, maybe just across the street from this pole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark with a cross where Mrs. Osmanovic was, firstly.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Would you like me to make a circle or a cross?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a cross.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Where Fatima Osmanovic was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now can you see in the photograph where Mrs. Kundo was or not?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: If I look at the photograph before me, yes, I can see it. It is a bit further up, above the pole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you place a small circle where Mrs. Kundo was when she was shot.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It could be somewhere here above this place because she was standing further down. Right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given where you have placed the circle, perhaps I should ask this question: Approximately how far apart were the two positions?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately a metre or two. Not more, because it was a fence through which there was a door and Ms. Ramiza would go through actually.
