The fence was demolished in one certain part so she didn't really have to go through the place where we would enter, but she could go through that part, so about a metre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the photograph at the top of the page and perhaps it could be slid down on the ELMO. You were asked questions during cross-examination about a place called, I think, Donje Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I know it as Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you were indicating during the questioning by Ms. Pilipovic, an area to the right of the black circle and towards the houses, and I think you indicated that area when you were asked to point to the area of Donje Polje or Donja Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: No -- yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take the same pen, that is the blue pen, and mark that area on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to indicate this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you actually see that area on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do see the area that I circled, so if I look at the picture on the right, you can see trees. I don't know what it is. So this is where the Polje is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so I can understand better, is there a particular area called Donje Polje?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that every -- that area beginning from Rajlovac is called Polje. Maybe there is an area called Donje Polje, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't take that any further. You were asked why you had not previously mentioned in your statement the incident involving Haska Dudevic, and you explained that you understand that she is seeking a pension; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Are there any other people that you know of and who you haven't told us about who were shot in that area?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I told you. Maybe you didn't understand me correctly. Muharem Mesanovic was also hit not far from here. The UNPROFOR was here and they were cleaning, trying to get rid of some garbage, and he was working for the Civil Defence and he was shot in the stomach and the UNPROFOR members brought him to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I remember you told us about him. I simply wanted to know, yes or no, were there any other people that were shot there that you know about, and perhaps I should also add that you saw shot; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr.President, I won't take that any further, given that this is re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since the question was asked with regards to whether this witness knows about other incidents and since my learned friend asked her to answer with a "yes" or "no," she answered "yes," I would just like to know if she could give us the names of these people and when these incidents occurred since this did not stem from the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Menzilovic, first, Ms. Pilipovic is asking whether she is allowed to put any additional questions. So if you would just like to wait. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't speak against that at all. If that is what the Defence wants to do, then naturally I am happy for the witness to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then please proceed. Further cross-examination by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question of my learned friend with regards to the fact whether you know if more people were wounded in that area and you said yes, could you tell us when incidents of this sort would have occurred, in what period of time, and do you know the names?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: I mentioned Muharem. There was also an older man, Moljo Mustafa. He is a neighbour. His house is next to my neighbour -- his house is next to my house, and he was also hit by a sniper. And he told me that he was wounded, however, he was very lucky not to be wounded in bone. And that is with regards to my neighbours. Now, for the others, I don't know if other people were wounded. I know that lots of people were wounded and died, but I don't know who they were exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when did this occur, in what year, in what month?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: With regards to Poljo Mustafa?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: It was somewhere in 1994, but I wouldn't really tell you the exact date. I wasn't really concerned by that. I just know that when he passed by, he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the beginning of 1994, was it at the end of 1994?

utterances.speaker: RASEMA MENZILOVIC
utterances.text: Please believe me that I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Ms. Menzilovic, you have answered the questions of the parties, so many questions that the judges have no further questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that this concludes your testimony in this Court. It has been quite a journey for you to come here to The Hague, and it is important for this Court to hear the answers of those who have been present during those days at those places, to hear their answers from questions both put by the Prosecution and by the Defence to the witnesses. So I therefore thank you very much for having come to The Hague, and I'll wish, first of all, that your headache is over, and apart from that, a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I was well treated here and I wish you all the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Usher, could you please escort Ms. Menzilovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3279X, 360-degree Quicktime movie; Exhibit P1812, photograph; Exhibit P1812A, two photographs marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. They are all admitted into evidence. I saw on your list, Mr. Ierace, that 1A to 11 mentioned before by Ms. Pilipovic was also mentioned -- it might have also created the confusion, but it has not been tendered. I am aware that your next witness will not take much time, at least so as it is indicated, that it was an quarter of an hour. Nevertheless, I am a bit hesitant to start because we have only ten minutes left and I asked already so many times the patience and the cooperation of the booth. I would rather not do it again. Are there any other issues? I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin started telling the Chamber that there was some progress and then I stopped him. If you want to tell us about the progress, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It is not necessary that I inform the Chamber of these progresses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anything else to -- well, then, I might have -- Madam Registrar, could you please assist me. Ask Mr. Usher, give one copy to both parties. I have got two copies. This is a form which should be used when there is any problem in respect of legibility of documents. It should be filled in the following way. The document number concerned. If it is not the whole document, those ERN pages it deals with. Then the third row needs some explanation. It says, "communicated to the counsel of the other party when." That means when has the complaint about illegibility recently, so I am not talking about a year ago, but when that has been recently brought to the attention of the other party, then when the answer was received, then why the answer is unsatisfactory, because that would cause the Chamber to deal with it. Whatever additional observations are to be made. The form also gives the opportunity to the other party if, for example, the Defence would complain about illegibility, that the Prosecution could write its comments on this form and then the form may be submitted to the Chamber. And the copies of the documents concerned or the pages, the ERN pages, should be attached to it. This is the way we are dealing with illegible or badly legible documents. The Chamber is not happy that it has to deal with it and for certain it is that better care could have been taken of providing legible documents. But nevertheless, whether we like it or not, the problem is often there and we would like to deal with it in an efficient way. So this is the form to be used, documents to be attached, give all the information, state what the answer of the other party is, why it is an unsatisfactory, give the other party to add what they want to add and it can be given to the other party. Mr. Piletta-Zanin

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence thanks the Chamber for your efforts by drafting and preparing this document, but the Defence nevertheless wishes to underline the following: Is the fact that we have to look through these documents to examine these documents, to sift through is a huge endeavour. It is an almost an impossible task that you are asking us to do. There are dozens, hundreds, maybe thousands, and for each of these documents we have to fill out a form, we will spend an incredible amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is good that you make the comment, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, because I might not have been clear enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This form is not meant in order to go through the thousands of documents, but is in order to deal with specifically those documents indicated on the list which is presented by the Prosecution, the list of documents that are going to be presented on short notice. So I would understand. I wouldn't ask from the Defence to go through 5.000 documents and to sift out whenever is illegible. But this is just in order to prevent that we are confronted with a problem of a specific document at the -- I have now got something quite new on my screen, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Technical difficulties sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have some technicians on my screen. But that is the way -- that is how we intend that the parties will use this form. As you might have noticed, this is the second form the Chamber has given to you. We always have taken it that if the Defence fills in no date and no crosses on the other form, that there are no problems as far as the disclosure of exhibits or whether in a good language has taken place similar to them from previous statements that are also mentioned on the other form. This new form, however, needs to be presented to the other party as well. So it is not just by filling in one party, it should be filled in by the other party as well. If there are no comments by the other party, just fill in none. Fine. Initials. We want to be sure about communication that has taken place before we are confronted with these type of problems in this courtroom. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will reiterate, I do thank the Chamber for its kind assistance. This will resolve in portion the problem that we have in terms of communicating with the Prosecution. But there are tens of thousands of documents that exist and there is some information in those documents that are useful for the Defence and if those documents are in the same illegible state that you have seen, well then we are hindered once again. We cannot trace back the elements that could be of any assistance to us because the documents are illegible. So I would like to reiterate our position. It is clear that all the documents such as medical documents, those documents are extremely important and they are either badly photocopied or they are completely illegible. We would ask for the production of the originals and this is when we will be able to see clearly what is going on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my friend has just referred to there being tens of thousands of documents. That makes clear that he is referring to reciprocal disclosure. The obligation of the Prosecution is to make available for inspection those documents, not to copy them. We have copied them. We have been criticised by the Defence for the quality of the copies. If my friend has any further complaints about documents which are given to him under a reciprocal disclosure obligation, not the documents we propose to tender, then the remedy is to inform us of the ERN number and he can inspect them. We will not provide further copies given the problems which under helpful cause under talk has not been acceded. Mr. President, might I raise one other related issue. Yesterday when I asked for the Defence to indicate how many copies of the documents that they complained about they had received, the Defence replied that they had received the documents in question yesterday on three occasions and they could not comment on the legibility of the copies given to them before December because they had destroyed them. There is an order still operating from the Pre-Trial Chamber from the year 2000 that all material which is provided to the Defence and which is not tendered, must be returned to the Prosecution. That is an order which operates in conjunction with another order, that the Defence is not to inform anyone, other than the accused, of the contents of the material which they receive, quite clearly without the leave of the Trial Chamber and there is a specific provision I think in relation to access by experts. Therefore, if that material has been destroyed, it should not have been destroyed because it is in contravention of an order, at least in terms of the future. It could seem from the order that it follows quite simply that if my friends don't have enough space to store this material Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and they want to get rid of it, because that is what they said yesterday, then they should return it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, terribly sorry, but I did not say yesterday that we have destroyed those documents. I only said that it is possible that and quite likely that they may have been destroyed. But I did not affirm before this Chamber that I had described the documents never --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, my first observation is that the Defence has repeatedly asked for originals to be provided to them. Under the disclosure obligations, the Prosecution is not under an obligation to provide originals of documents of which they only have copies. If there would be a very specific issue on which the Defence has a specific interest on having originals, apart from that, they can inspect the documents as they are in the hands of the Prosecution, they could always ask whether the Prosecution could assist in getting the originals. But then of course it should be a very specific reason because it goes beyond the obligations of the Prosecution. That is number one. The second observation I would like to make is that I always understood that if material has to be returned to the Prosecution, that is, in order to prevent that it will remain in the hands of the other party, I don't know whether the rule and whether the order says something specific on repeatedly provided documents. So I would not say it is as clear as what to do with other documents which are the same ones that provided before. But perhaps if these are large quantities of documents and not just one or two pieces of paper which you could put in a shredder, then perhaps the Defence then gets in touch with the Prosecution and see whether the other ones can be returned. I again took three minutes from the booth. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, same time.
